rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies night and day with the moon and sun; the moon’s waning after fullness is the erasure of its light.
rows.anchor: المراد وجعلنا نيري الليل والنهر آيتين يريد الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the erasure as lunar markings; a report says Gabriel passed his wing over the moon and removed its light.
rows.anchor: المراد من محو القمر الكلف الذي يظهر في وجهه يروى أن الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, erasure means removing a trace, as in the verbs for wiping something away.
rows.anchor: تقول : محوته أمحوه وانمحى وامتحى إذا ذهب أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers lunar waxing and waning: its changing light affects worldly conditions and produces lunar months and Arabic years used for reckoning.
rows.anchor: حمل المحو في هذه الآية على الوجه الأول أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even lunar markings would show a voluntary Creator: a simple, uniform moon cannot explain why dim matter occupies only some parts without deliberate specification.
rows.anchor: فحصول الأحوال المختلفة الحاصلة بسبب المحو يدل على أنه ليس بسبب الطبيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Enlightening” can mean luminous, naming the effect of light—seeing—for its cause.
rows.anchor: معنى كونها مبصرة أي مضيئة وذلك لأن الإضاءة سبب لحصول الإبصار

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda reads “the day is enlightening” as saying its people can see during it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة يقال : قد أبصر النهار إذا صار الناس يبصرون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day provide rest and livelihood, as other verses also say.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى ذكر في آيات كثيرة منافع الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight lets people see how to conduct their work; reckoning covers hours, days, and months, while years are counted as a separate rank.
rows.anchor: الحساب مبني على أربع مراتب : الساعات والأيام والشهور والسنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained everything people need for religious and worldly interests, fully detailing the signs and benefits in night and day.
rows.anchor: كل شيء بكم إليه حاجة في مصالح دينكم ودنياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added verbal noun “in detail” reinforces and confirms the statement.
rows.anchor: لأجل تأكيد الكلام وتقريره ، كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage follows the completed explanation of signs and warning: because revelation has removed excuses, each person will face a record and answer for deeds.
rows.anchor: كل ما يحتاج إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد فقد صار مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second link is that God’s provision of worldly and religious benefits entails that people should serve and obey Him, so their deeds are questioned.
rows.anchor: وذلك يقتضي وجوب اشتغالهم بخدمته وطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third link is that creation is for worship; the sun, moon, night, and day enable obedience, which is then assessed at resurrection.
rows.anchor: فلما شرح أحوال الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab omen-taking from birds’ direction and manner of flight led “bird/omen” to signify a person’s good or evil deeds; this is supported by the reading of Hasan and Mujahid.
rows.anchor: قراءة الحسن ومجاهد : { ألزمناه طئره فى عنقه }

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says “bird” means a person’s lot or fortune, called bakht in Persian.
rows.anchor: الطائر عند العرب الحظ وهو الذي تسميه الفرس البخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains the assigned “bird” as each person’s decreed share of intellect, lifespan, provision, and felicity or misery, which inevitably reaches them.
rows.anchor: كل ما قدره الله تعالى ومضى في علمه حصوله ، فهو لازم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The binding of the assigned deed supports the claim that whatever God decrees in prior knowledge must occur and cannot fail to occur.
rows.anchor: كل ما قدره الله تعالى للإنسان وحكم عليه به في سابق علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues first that an assigned deed is necessarily obtained because what is made binding cannot be removed.
rows.anchor: وما كان لازما للشيء كان ممتنع الزوال عنه واجب الحصول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues second that God explicitly attributes the binding to Himself, comparing it with binding people to piety.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية دالة على أنه لا يظهر في الأبد إلا ما حكم الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying that the Pen has dried concerning what will occur until Resurrection reinforces the decree argument; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: جف القلم بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “On his neck” is an idiom for an obligation assigned to someone, like placing a task or responsibility in one’s neck as a collar.
rows.anchor: كناية عن اللزوم كما يقال : جعلت هذا في عنقك

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The neck is singled out because good deeds adorn their bearer like jewelry, while sins disgrace and shackle like a collar.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص العنق من بين سائر الأعضاء بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says two recording angels preserve good deeds on the right and sins on the left; after death the record is folded and kept with the person until it is brought out at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يا ابن آدم بسطنا لك صحيفة ووكل بك ملكان فهما عن يمينك وشمالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We bring it out for him” can mean bringing the hidden record from the grave when the person is raised.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون معناه : نخرج له ذلك لأنه لم ير كتابه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads the verb in the passive, understood as the person’s deed or “bird” being brought out as an opened book.
rows.anchor: أي يخرج له الطائر أي عمله كتابا منشورا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reads “he meets it” as “he is handed it,” by analogy with language for presenting something to someone.
rows.anchor: من قولهم : لقيت فلانا الشيء أي استقبلته به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unstated speaker—God through the angels—tells the person to read the book.
rows.anchor: وهذا القائل هو الله تعالى على ألسنة الملائكة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the person reads the record whether literate or illiterate.
rows.anchor: يقرؤه أميا كان أو غير أمي

rows.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Bakr ibn Abd Allah describes a believer reading good deeds displayed on the record’s back and sins inside, then receiving private forgiveness and great joy.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بالمؤمن يوم القيامة بصحيفته وهو يقرؤها وحسناته في ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Accountant” means the person himself will reckon and audit his deeds.
rows.anchor: كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan calls it just that God makes each person their own accountant.
rows.anchor: عدل والله في حقك من جعلك حسيب نفسك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the disbeliever asks to judge himself in light of God’s declaration that He is not unjust to servants.
rows.anchor: يقول الكافر يومئذ إنك قضيت أنك لست بظلام للعبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s deeds resemble birds flying toward them because God’s eternal decree of good and evil must reach each person; recognizing this shows the need for eternal divine care.
rows.anchor: قدر لكل أحد في الأزل مقدارا من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every event is preceded by another event in a chain established by God, like countless birds launched from pre-eternity toward a particular person, time, and condition.
rows.anchor: جعل لكل حادث حادثا متقدما عليه لحصول الحادث المتأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated voluntary acts form stable habits in the soul; each act leaves an effect, as repeated water drops eventually bore a stone.
rows.anchor: تكرار الأعمال الاختيارية تفيد حدوث الملكة النفسانية الراسخة في جوهر النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because conventional letters merely signify sounds by human agreement while soul-impressions are essential and lasting, the latter better deserve the name “book.”
rows.anchor: دلالة تلك النقوش على تلك المعاني المخصوصة دلالة كائنة جوهرية واجبة الثبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed leaves a trace in the soul: attraction from creation toward God brings felicity, while attraction away from God toward created things brings misery.
rows.anchor: كل عمل يصدر من الإنسان كثيرا كان أو قليلا قويا كان أو ضعيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The body’s governance hides these traces; when its bond ends at death, the soul rises and the Resurrection begins in this spiritual sense.
rows.anchor: من مات فقد قامت قيامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened book is the soul’s previously hidden worldly impressions, now exposed after bodily attachment ends and read by the intellect.
rows.anchor: ونخرج له عند حصول هذه القيامة من عمق البدن المظلم كتابا مشتملا على جميع تلك الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this spiritual interpretation, the person’s own soul-impressions reveal whether their effects entail felicity or misery.
rows.anchor: فإن تلك الآثار إن كانت من موجبات السعادة حصلت السعادة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi affirms the apparent narrated events as true while allowing the spiritual interpretations; he calls affirming both the sound, straight approach.
rows.anchor: الأحوال الظاهرة التي وردت فيها الروايات حق وصدق لا مرية فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse restates that each person is responsible for their own deeds and that good or evil consequences do not pass to someone else.
rows.anchor: كل أحد مختص بعمل نفسه

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi argues that the verse implies human ability to choose good or evil rather than compulsion to one act.
rows.anchor: الآية دالة على أن العبد متمكن من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the root of “burden” as sin and gives two readings: no one bears another’s sin, and no one may sin on the excuse that others did.
rows.anchor: يقال وزر يزر فهو وازر ووزر وزرا وزرة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi argues that children are not punished for their parents’ disbelief, since that would make them bear another’s sin.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي في الآية دلالة على أنه تعالى لا يعذب الأطفال بكفر آبائهم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits a Prophetic report that a dead person is punished for relatives’ wailing; Aisha challenges its soundness by citing this verse. Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: روى ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi argues sin is not created by God: otherwise a person could be punished for it as for another’s sin, and only voluntary, avoidable conduct is culpable.
rows.anchor: دلت هذه الآية على أن الوزر والإثم ليس من فعل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some early jurists reject charging blood money to a person’s agnates because that burdens them with another’s act; the reply says this is an initial divine duty and the mistaken killer is not culpable for it.
rows.anchor: أن جماعة من قدماء الفقهاء امتنعوا من ضرب الدية على العاقلة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s theologians say reason alone does not establish an obligation to thank the benefactor: obligation requires possible punishment, and this verse denies punishment before revelation.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا وجوب شكر المنعم لا يثبت بالعقل بل بالسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An opposing argument says denial of rational duties also undermines revealed duties, because one must rationally examine a claimant’s prophetic proof rather than rely on a circular or regress-prone revealed command.
rows.anchor: إذا جاء المشرع وادعى كونه نبيا من عند الله تعالى وأظهر المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same argument says commands and prohibitions depend on threatened punishment, so rational avoidance of harm must already be obligatory or obligation becomes circular.
rows.anchor: لو تركت كذا وفعلت كذا لعاقبتك فنقول : إما أن يجب عليه الاحتراز عن العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It further argues that even if God may forgive, obligation involves fear of punishment, and reason alone produces that fear and thus rational obligation.
rows.anchor: مذهب أهل السنة أنه يجوز من الله تعالى أن يعفو عن العقاب على ترك الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply says fear of blame also establishes rational obligation, since the possibility of divine pardon removes blame but not the rational fear that grounds obligation.
rows.anchor: ماهية الوجوب إنما تتقرر بسبب حصول الخوف من الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes “messenger” as reason itself, the original messenger that makes recognition of prophetic messengers possible.
rows.anchor: العقل هو رسول الله إلى الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation restricts the verse to duties knowable only through revelation; Razi says the apparent general wording may be specified when proofs require it.
rows.anchor: المراد وما كنا معذبين في الأعمال التي لا سبيل إلى معرفة وجوبها إلا بالشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi’s own view is that reason obliges people to seek benefit and avoid harm, but it cannot impose duties on God, who needs neither benefit nor protection from harm.
rows.anchor: مجرد العقل سبب في أن يجب علينا فعل ما ينتفع به ، وترك ما يتضرر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority says God commanded the affluent to do good, but they defiantly disobeyed; Razi rejects al-Zamakhshari’s reading that God commanded them to sin, since disobedience is contrary to a command.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : أن المراد منه الأمر بالفعل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead says the wording appears to command sin but metaphorically means that abundant comfort made the affluent rebel; Razi calls this plainly unsound.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ظاهر اللفظ يدل على أنه تعالى يأمرهم بالفسق

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: A second interpretation reads the verb as “We made them numerous”; al-Wahidi reports that Arabic usage can mean a people increased in number.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : العرب تقول أمر القوم إذا كثروا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda supports the “made numerous” sense with a Prophetic saying about a prolific foal and a well-built saddle; others instead interpret the foal as ordered to breed.
rows.anchor: واحتج أبو عبيدة على صحة هذه اللغة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( خير المال مهرة مأمورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent are those whose comfort has made them insolent; they disobey God, deserve the sentence of punishment, and are totally destroyed.
rows.anchor: وأما المترف : فمعناه في اللغة المتنعم الذي قد أبطرته النعمة وسعة العيش

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi’s theologians infer that God wills harm initially, singles out the affluent knowing they will sin, and has decreed their punishment so their later faith is impossible.
rows.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على صحة مذهبهم من وجوه

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi rejects initiating harm and reads this passage alongside verses that make human change, gratitude, or wrongdoing precede punishment, including the immediately preceding verse.
rows.anchor: قال الكعبي : إن سائر الآيات دلت على أنه تعالى لا يبتدىء بالتعذيب

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal’s first reconciliation says God does not punish people merely for foreknown disobedience: He commands the affluent to believe and obey, then punishes after their sin becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: قال إنه تعالى أخبر أنه لا يعذب أحدا بما يعلمه منه ما لم يعمل به

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal’s second reconciliation says God delays punishment and repeatedly calls the abundantly blessed affluent to repent; their continued defiance leads to destruction.
rows.anchor: لم نعاجلها بالعذاب في أول ظهور المعاصي منهم

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says God exhausts excuses before punishing: after sending a messenger He continues admonition, then destroys those who persist, as illustrated by Noah and other peoples.
rows.anchor: لا يعاجل بالعقوبة أمة ظالمة حتى يعذر إليهم غاية الأعذار

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi reads “when We willed” as “when the time of destruction approached,” not as willing destruction before sin; he compares it with a patient nearing death or a trader nearing ruin.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد من الآية أنه تعالى يريد إهلاكهم قبل أن يعصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the three predestinarian arguments depart from the wording’s apparent sense, though the second and third withstand the objections raised against them.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن جميع الوجوه الثلاثة التي ذكرناها في التمسك بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: القراء السبعة
rows.claim: The seven canonical readers use the unlengthened, light form; an uncommon report from Nafi and Ibn Abbas lengthens it, while Abu Amr doubles it.
rows.anchor: المشهور عند القراء السبعة : { أمرنا مترفيها } بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lengthening gives the sense “made them numerous”; doubling means giving the affluent free rein by removing restraint.
rows.anchor: فالمد على الكثير يقال : أمر القوم بكسر الميم إذا كثروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past destroyed peoples after Noah—such as ʿĀd and Thamud—show this is God’s established way with rebellious peoples; the address to the Prophet warns everyone.
rows.anchor: وهم عاد وثمود وغيرهم ، ثم إنه تعالى خاطب رسوله بما يكون خطابا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge, power to repay justly, and freedom from injustice reassure the obedient and terrify disbelievers and sinners.
rows.anchor: ومجموع هذه الصفات الثلاث أعني العلم التام ، والقدرة الكاملة ، والبراءة عن الظلم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the preposition bāʾ may enter the subject in an expression of praise or blame, as in “suffices you by him”; without praise or blame it is not used this way.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : لو ألغيت الباء من قولك بربك جاز

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal connects this verse to each person’s assigned “bird”: those seeking only worldly status may reject the prophets, yet receive only what God wills and end in Hell.
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : هذه الآية داخلة في معنى قوله : { وكل إنسان ألزمناه طئره فى عنقه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell’s wording depicts punishment as lasting harm with humiliation and exile from divine mercy, without relief or escape.
rows.anchor: العقاب عبارة عن مضرة مقرونة بالإهانة والذم بشرط أن تكون دائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly success should not be mistaken for God’s approval: it may end in punishment, and a person’s deeds can drive them like an ill omen toward torment.
rows.anchor: مساعدة الدنيا لا ينبغي أن يستدل بها على رضا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “for whom We will” warns that many who abandon religion for worldly gain obtain neither; they are the greatest losers despite thinking they act well.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه لا يحصل الفوز بالدنيا لكل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first condition is intending the afterlife’s reward; without that intention an act does not benefit, as the verse about human striving and the saying about intentions indicate.
rows.anchor: الشرط الأول : أن يريد بعمله الآخرة أي ثواب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intention matters because the purpose of deeds is to illuminate the heart through knowing and loving God, which requires intending worship and obedience.
rows.anchor: المقصود من الأعمال استنارة القلب بمعرفة الله تعالى ومحبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second condition is pursuing the afterlife by valid acts of worship; idolatrous approaches remain invalid even when their practitioners intend devotion.
rows.anchor: أن يكون العمل الذي يتوصل به إلى الفوز بثواب الآخرة من الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some idolaters claim they cannot worship God directly, so they worship stars or angels as devoted intermediaries; Razi rejects this as invalid.
rows.anchor: يقولون : إله العالم أجل وأعظم من أن يقدر الواحد منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say their idols depict prophets and saints and are meant to secure their intercession; Razi also rejects this path.
rows.anchor: والتأويل الثاني لهم : أنهم قالوا : نحن اتخذنا هذه التماثيل على صور الأنبياء والأولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also reports that people in India seek closeness to God by killing or burning themselves, but says this too is an invalid route.
rows.anchor: وأيضا نقل عن الهند : أنهم يتقربون إلى الله تعالى بقتل أنفسهم تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is the third condition; without it acts of piety do not earn reward, while meeting all three conditions makes the effort appreciated and accepted.
rows.anchor: وهذا الشرط معتبر ، لأن الشرط في كون أعمال البر موجبة للثواب تقدم الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude comprises recognizing the recipient as a benefactor, praising them verbally, and acting in ways that honor them; God treats the obedient in all three ways.
rows.anchor: الشكر عبارة عن مجموع أمور ثلاثة : اعتقاد كونه محسنا في تلك الأعمال

rows.speaker: جعفر بن حرب
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Harb argues that faith must be created by God because otherwise thanking God for it would be improper praise for another’s act.
rows.anchor: رأيت في كتب المعتزلة أن جعفر بن حرب حضر عنده واحد من أهل السنة وقال : الدليل على أن الإيمان حصل بخلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ثمامة بن الأشرس
rows.claim: Thumama replies that people thank God for the capacity, intellect, revealed books, and proofs He provides, while God thanks them for the faith they perform.
rows.anchor: فدخل ثمامة بن الأشرس وقال : إنما نمدح الله تعالى ونشكره على ما أعطانا من القدرة والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reconciles the positions: God supplies the complete power and motive, while the servant performs the act of faith, so both God and servant can rightly receive thanks.
rows.anchor: مجموع القدرة مع الداعي يوجب الفعل كلام واضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He classifies actions by whether they aim at worldly good, afterlife good, both together, or neither; the verse directly treats the first two.
rows.anchor: فإما أن يقصد بذلك الفعل تحصيل خيرات الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When afterlife motive outweighs worldly motive, Razi presents disagreement: a divine report rejects works involving association, while one analysis denies purity if motives combine and another accepts the dominant afterlife motive.
rows.anchor: أنا أغنى الأغنياء عن الشرك من عمل عملا أشرك فيه غيري تركته وشريكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equal motives or a stronger worldly motive are agreed to make the act unaccepted, though either is better than seeking worldly benefit alone.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا كان طلب الدنيا وطلب الآخرة متعادلين ، أو كان طلب الدنيا راجحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On acting without any motive, those who require a motive say it cannot occur; those who do not require one deem it inwardly ineffective and outwardly forbidden as pointless.
rows.anchor: هذا بناء على أن صدور الفعل من القادر هل يتوقف على حصول الداعي أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies both groups with worldly wealth, children, and adornments because His gift is ample for all; He gives each what wisdom requires to remove excuses in this life of action.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى يمد الفريقين بالأموال ويوسع عليهما في الرزق مثل الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of “how We favored some” concerns unequal worldly provision among believers and unbelievers, as God apportions livelihood for people to serve one another and tests them.
rows.anchor: انظر إلى عطائنا المباح إلى الفريقين في الدنيا ، كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since worldly ranks differ visibly, afterlife ranks differ even more; desire for the greater, lasting distinction should exceed desire for worldly rank.
rows.anchor: أن تفاضل الخلق في درجات منافع الدنيا محسوس ، فتفاضلهم في درجات منافع الآخرة أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading says the afterlife is greater because believers enter Paradise and disbelievers enter Hell, making their difference manifest.
rows.anchor: فيظهر فضل المؤمنين على الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage develops the preceding conditions for afterlife success: it begins with faith, whose noblest part is affirming divine unity and rejecting partners.
rows.anchor: وأشرف أجزاء الإيمان هو التوحيد ونفي الشركاء والأضداد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes take the prohibition as addressed outwardly to the Prophet but applying generally to all morally responsible people.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : هذا في الظاهر خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers reading the addressee as humankind, since the following instruction about aged parents does not fit the Prophet’s parents.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاحتمال عندي أولى ، لأنه تعالى عطف عليه قوله : { وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheist deserves blame for falsehood and for attributing some blessings to nonexistent partners instead of thanking God, the true source of all blessings.
rows.anchor: المشرك كاذب والكاذب يستوجب الذم والخذلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By assigning a partner authority, the polytheist is left without a helper when that partner proves nonexistent; affirming multiplicity also chooses imperfection over unity.
rows.anchor: لما كان ذلك الشريك معدوما بقي بلا ناصر ولا حافظ ولا معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Remain seated” can mean simply remain in a condition, whether standing or sitting, as Arabic and Persian usage illustrate.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن معناه : المكث أي فتمكث في الناس مذموما مخذولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it evokes the remorseful posture of someone blamed and abandoned.
rows.anchor: إن من شأن المذموم المخذول أن يقعد نادما متفكرا على ما فرط منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation makes standing a metaphor for capacity to pursue good and sitting a metaphor for helplessness and inability to pursue it.
rows.anchor: جعل القيام كناية عن القدرة على تحصيل الخيرات . والقعود كناية عن العجز والضعف

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the subjunctive after the prohibitive faʾ has an implied “an”; grammarians call it a response because the second action follows from the first.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : قوله : ( فتقعد ) انتصب لأنه وقع بعد الفاء جوابا للنهي
